chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, I have transmitted from my father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah and al-Himyari together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam.
His kunyah was Abu Muhammad, he was a mawla of Banu Shayban, a seller of woolen garments, and he moved from Baghdad to Kufa.

key_terms.بَيَّاعُ الْكَرَابِيسِ: A seller of woolen garments or coarse cloth.
key_terms.تَحَوَّلَ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ إِلَى الْكُوفَة: He relocated from Baghdad to Kufa.
key_terms.مَوْلَى بَنِي شَيْبَانَ: A client or freedman affiliated with Banu Shayban.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Hisham ibn al-Hakam in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih, and who was he?
ai.summary: This passage gives the transmission chain through which the author narrates reports from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, then provides brief biographical details about him. It is significant for hadith transmission and rijal literature, identifying his kunyah, tribal affiliation as a mawla, profession, and relocation from Baghdad to Kufa.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam has been transmitted by me from my father and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah (swt) be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Al-Himyari together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam.
His kunya was Abu Muhammad, and he was a freed servant (mawla) of Banu Shayban. He was a seller of woolen garments and moved from Baghdad to Kufa.
